remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was added; the Actor only narrowed the characterization of BPROC-012-C, BPROC-012-D, and BPROC-012-E.
The policy requires admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk to support rejection, and the record still lacks a logged materiality assessment or equivalent approval-bar criterion.

BPROC-012-E supports follow-up before approval if storage controls remain unresolved, but it does not show that the issue was formally unresolved at decision time or that rejection was the required outcome.
BPROC-012-D expressly says no failed control test is logged, so the packet remains vulnerable if it is read as establishing more than inconsistency plus unresolved diligence.
The Actor's 'approval conditions were not affirmatively satisfied' framing is not itself evidenced by a documented approval standard in the record.
final_rationale: The verdict remains suspicious. The Actor improved the packet by narrowing it to a caveated, risk-based rationale and by conceding that the evidence does not prove a control failure or an express rejection mandate. That helps avoid overclaiming, but it does not satisfy the missing compliance predicate. Under the policy text, rejection must rest on admissible evidence showing a material unresolved risk. The available record shows a questionnaire variance (BPROC-012-D), a recommendation for follow-up before approval if unresolved (BPROC-012-E), and weak process documentation (BPROC-012-C). Those items support follow-up or escalation and can support a conservative concern narrative, but on this record alone they still do not clearly establish materiality or a formally unresolved condition sufficient to make rejection compliant. The Actor's shift is therefore a reframing of the same evidence, not a genuine evidentiary change.
